Ben Macdui.credit: Mick Knapton at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0
Ben Macdui.about: Britain's second-highest mountain: a vast stony plateau with a view indicator, said to be haunted by the Big Grey Man, Am Fear Liath Mòr.

routes.name: From the Cairn Gorm ski centre
routes.text: From the Coire Cas car park, up the ridge of Fiacaill a' Choire Chais, then across the plateau past Lochan Buidhe. Navigation is serious in mist.

routes.name: Linn of Dee via Derry Lodge
routes.text: Ride the estate track to Derry Lodge, then walk up Glen Luibeg and the long Sròn Riach ridge or by Loch Etchachan.

Braeriach.about: Britain's third-highest summit, perched on the rim of huge corries above the Lairig Ghru. The River Dee rises at the Wells of Dee on its plateau.

routes.name: Chalamain Gap
routes.text: From the Sugar Bowl car park on the ski road, through the bouldery Chalamain Gap, down into the Lairig Ghru and up the Sròn na Lairige ridge.

routes.name: Gleann Einich
routes.text: Ride the long Gleann Einich track from Whitewell or Coylumbridge, then up Coire Dhondail onto the plateau and round the corrie rim.

Cairn Toul.about: A pointed summit on the west rim of the Lairig Ghru, Britain's fourth-highest, usually climbed with Braeriach and the Angel's Peak.

routes.name: From Braeriach
routes.text: Round the rim of the plateau and over the Angel's Peak: the classic high Cairngorm traverse.

routes.name: Corrour Bothy
routes.text: From Linn of Dee via Derry Lodge and the Lairig Ghru to Corrour Bothy, then up the Coire Odhar path to the ridge.

Sgor an Lochain Uaine.about: The Angel's Peak: a sharp top above the green lochan of Garbh Choire, between Braeriach and Cairn Toul.

routes.name: Braeriach to Cairn Toul
routes.text: Climbed on the traverse between them, from Braeriach round the corrie rim or a short climb from the col with Cairn Toul.

Cairn Gorm.about: The mountain that names the range, above the ski area, with a weather station on top and the Ptarmigan station of the funicular railway just below.

routes.name: Windy Ridge
routes.text: From the Coire Cas car park up the Sròn an Aonaich ridge beside the ski tows, past the Ptarmigan station to the summit.

routes.name: Northern corries
routes.text: Up Fiacaill a' Choire Chais and round the cliff tops of Coire an t-Sneachda, a fine high circuit.

Beinn a' Bhùird.about: A huge flat-topped mountain in the eastern Cairngorms, ringed by fine corries; the North Top is its highest point.

routes.name: Glen Quoich and An Diollaid
routes.text: From the car park at Allanaquoich, up Glen Quoich, then the path on the line of the old Land Rover road up An Diollaid to the plateau and north to the top. Often biked to the start of the climb.

routes.name: Quoich Water to The Sneck
routes.text: Through the pinewoods along the Quoich Water to The Sneck, the col with Ben Avon.

Beinn Mheadhoin.credit: Mick Knapton at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0
Beinn Mheadhoin.about: The 'middle hill': a remote plateau studded with granite tors between Loch Avon and Loch Etchachan.

routes.name: From the Cairn Gorm ski centre
routes.text: Across the plateau and down to the head of Loch Avon by the Shelter Stone, then up past Loch Etchachan.

routes.name: Linn of Dee via Glen Derry
routes.text: Ride to Derry Lodge, walk up Glen Derry to Loch Etchachan, then up the broad south-west slope.

Ben Avon.about: A sprawling plateau dotted with granite tors. The top, Leabaidh an Daimh Bhuidhe, is a tor you must scramble up to touch the highest point.

routes.name: Via The Sneck
routes.text: Up the glen between Ben Avon and Beinn a' Bhùird to The Sneck, the col between them; often combined with Beinn a' Bhùird.

routes.name: Gleann an t-Slugain
routes.text: From Keiloch near Braemar, the track through Gleann an t-Slugain (good on a bike), then the long southern slopes, passing close to the rim of the Slochd Mòr corrie.

routes.name: Glen Avon
routes.text: From Tomintoul along the long Glen Avon track; one of the remotest approaches in the Cairngorms.

Beinn Bhrotain.about: A broad, bouldery dome at the south end of the Cairn Toul ridge, above Glen Dee and Glen Geusachan.

routes.name: Linn of Dee via White Bridge
routes.text: Ride the track to the White Bridge and up Glen Dee, then climb the south-east slopes. Often combined with Monadh Mòr.

Lochnagar.about: The royal mountain above Balmoral: a great cliff-ringed corrie and loch beneath a summit ridge whose top is Cac Càrn Beag.

routes.name: Spittal of Glenmuick
routes.text: Up the track to the col below Meikle Pap, then the steep 'Ladder' path and round the rim of the corrie.

routes.name: Circuit via the Glas Allt
routes.text: Return down past the Glas Allt falls to Loch Muick for a fine round.
